subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status --deep` report live gateway memory runtime health for plugin-owned memory, or should it continue to show skipped/inconclusive memory state unless `--all` or `openclaw memory status --deep` is used?
rationale: Both directions are plausible: live gateway health better matches the report, while keeping status mostly passive avoids plugin side effects and overlaps with the broader local-probe issue.

options.title: Add live runtime health
options.body: Repair or replace the open closing PR with a focused runtime-vs-embedding payload contract and human/JSON status coverage.

options.title: Keep passive status
options.body: Close or retarget the open closing PR and clarify docs that memory plugin health is intentionally checked through `--all` or `openclaw memory status --deep`.

options.title: Fold into broader side-effect work
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical fix path if maintainers want to redesign status probing more broadly.

recommendation.title: Add live runtime health
recommendation.body: Repair or replace the open closing PR with a focused runtime-vs-embedding payload contract and human/JSON status coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best current owner signal from recent status/memory reporting work and the product boundary around plugin status behavior.
